title: Hybrid size+timeout fairness experiment runbook
body:
Purpose:
This runbook documents a targeted set of experiments that evaluate a hybrid scheduler policy (size-first + adaptive timeout) to improve p95/p99 tail latency while preserving fairness across tenant priority classes and maintaining throughput. Goal is a practical policy we can A/B in staging and, if successful, roll into canary for Dedicated clusters.

Background/context:
- Prior experiments (see linked artifacts) showed gains from continuous batching but exposed worst-case tail amplification for small high-priority requests when queue timeouts favor throughput.
- We need a policy that reduces tail spikes for latency-sensitive requests (interactive small prompts) without blowing up cost/throughput for throughput-oriented workloads (long-batch embeddings).

Key hypotheses:
1) A size-first base ordering (group by token-length buckets) reduces variance for long requests but starves small requests; adding an adaptive per-priority timeout will allow small requests to bypass when their wait exceeds a fast threshold, improving p99 for high-priority traffic.
2) Making the adaptive timeout token-aware (shorter timeouts when KV-cache miss predicted) further reduces waste and improves P90-99 for mixed workloads.
3) Fairness (min-share guarantees per tenant) enforced on top of hybrid policy limits starvation to under 5% degraded requests for lower-tier tenants.

Experiment design:
- Testbed: 3 identical staging clusters (g4dn-like profile); each cluster runs the full runtime with scheduler variant enabled via feature flag.
- Workload generator: synthetic mix of 3 traffic classes generated from historical traces (sampled):
  * interactive-small (50–200 tokens, 60% of requests, 45% of total token volume) - priority HIGH
  * standard-medium (200–1k tokens, 30% requests) - priority NORMAL
  * bulk-long (1k–8k tokens, 10% requests, high token volume) - priority LOW
- Key metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (enqueue-to-first-token), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, queue length distribution, fairness violation rate (requests whose service time violated min-share SLA), cost-per-1M-tokens estimate.
- Observability hooks: tracing to attach scheduler-decision reason to spans, per-request token-count tag, KV-cache-hit boolean, sample flamegraphs from runtime (hot functions: batch-assemble, kv-cache-lookup, scheduler-dequeue).

Scheduler variants (feature-flag names):
- baseline_continuous: current production continuous batching (time-based batching with global timeout 8ms, FIFO-ish within time window).
- variant_size_first: order by predicted token-length descending then fill batches up to size cap; global timeout 12ms to favor bigger batches.
